newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dollar vols cut gains after spike up.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dollar vols cut gains after spike up.

text.p: Implied volatilities for short-dated dollar-pair options had cut their biggest gains by Tuesday afternoon but mainly stayed above Monday's midday levels as the market settled in for Japan's Tankan report.
Although many analysts looked for Tankan to depict a still-weak economy, not all pundits agreed about the timbre of the report, which they said could rouse the market.

"We've heard some mixed forecasts on the market," said one OTC options broker of the Tankan report. "I think this could be a source (of direction). A strong or weak number could cause some vol mixup."

Tuesday afternoon, one-month dollar/yen was quoted at 10.75/11.00 percent, off from 11.0/11.5 percent in early European trading but up from 10.15/10.45 Monday and near last Friday afternoon's pre-Group of Seven summit levels.
The 25-delta risk reversal still strongly favored yen calls, at about 1.9/2.4 points, up slightly from Monday's 1.7/2.1 points but off from 2.2/2.4 points quoted last Friday.

Volatilities had scurried higher late Monday as the dollar briefly skidded to 114.00 yen area and U.S. blue-chip stocks tumbled after comments by Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, which Japan later said were misinterpreted.
But the spike up lacked durability, and vols for many front-end options had stabilized as the dollar regained its footing in surprising calm trade, brokers said.
"Since that dollar spike, they've come off a ton...about four vols in one-month," said the OTC broker.
"I think they were looking for more fallout from the Japan thing, the Dow Jones (index drop) and all that," said one options floor broker at the International Monetary Market.
"I don't think anybody took it (Hashimoto remarks) as a serious threat. It kind of got brushed aside," the OTC options broker said.
Cable volatility edged up, but trade also stayed quiet even though sterling probed below 1.6630 support after Goldman Sachs said the pound was overvalued by about 15 percent.

"The vols perked up. July, which is only about one week, is above nine percent," said the IMM floor broker. "It hasn't been up there for a while. But the one-month (August) is only up a little bit. It's about 8.2 percent, which is up less than a half-point."
"I think vols are up gradually, but they're not really popping," agreed the OTC broker of sterling.
The IMM August dollar/mark 25-delta call straddle was quoted at about 8.8 percent, a hair above Monday's level, the floor broker said.
One-month OTC marks stood at 8.35/8.55 percent Tuesday afternoon, little changed from 8.45/8.70 percent in early Europe and compared to 8.20/8.50 percent Monday afternoon.
"Everything's pretty quiet," added the OTC broker. "I think it's more a function of people are really unsure of the next direction." ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
